newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Euro derivatives to be more like U.S. - conference.
newsitem.headline: Euro derivatives to be more like U.S. - conference.

text.p: The introduction of a single European currency will make derivatives markets in Europe more professional and sophisticated, a conference heard on Monday.
Dr Jan Sybrand, head of risk management at Dutch bank ABN AMRO in Amsterdam, said European futures markets were less liquid and less precise than those of the United States.
But this would change with the advent of the Euro currency in 1999.
"Continental Europe will turn into a dollar-sized, dollar type market," he told a seminar on the first day of the two-day Amsterdam Derivatives Forum.
He also said over-the-counter trading would drive European futures markets, giving them a big boost, once the Euro was introduced.
Sybrand said however derivatives traders in Europe would become much more concerned with relative value and arbitrage opportunities than with market direction.
He said U.S. markets were characterised by higher volumes and lower margins than Europe's markets, which offer bigger risks and bigger rewards.
Sybrand gave as an example the Netherlands, which does not have a liquid bond futures contract.
This forces investors to use German futures markets for hedging, leaving themselves open to currency and interest rate risks.
"It's a very erratic way of covering the guilder market," he said.
